name: Bioinformatics
boundaries: Bioinformatics: fundamental discoveries and enabling technologies within this field. Include cross-field consequences where the central advance belongs to this field; exclude routine incremental optimization. Use the historical breakthroughs in the prompt to calibrate revolutionary impact.

original_dispositions.reason: Covered by BIF-03 and BIF-04, with spatial integration in BIF-07. The useful underlying goals are causal and perturbation-predictive models using appropriate modalities. Arbitrary inputs, zero information loss, elimination of all batch effects and an actionable patient twin are not assumed.

original_dispositions.original_title: Perfect single-cell trajectory inference and future-state prediction
original_dispositions.reason: The revised concept uses calibrated probabilities and recognizes intrinsic uncertainty.
Covered by BIF-01 and BIF-04, with broader intervention behavior in BIF-03. Specified context and measurements replace an assumption that sequence alone determines all dynamics.
The proposed test is reproducible discovery across problems; the unsupported 100–1000× acceleration claim is omitted.

original_dispositions.original_title: Polynomial-time perfect de novo assembly of any eukaryotic genome
original_dispositions.reason: Added in revised form. The transformative accessibility goal remains; universal perfection and reconstruction from insufficient reads do not.
Added as BIF-09, overlapping BIF-02. Experimental and clinical validation remain necessary.
Added in revised form as BIF-12, with gene-function decoding also in BIF-06. Claims are bounded by detection, measurement and identifiability.

Covered substantially by BIF-01, with causal mechanisms in BIF-04. BIF-01 includes context and splicing, but the present evidence does not establish a complete predictive grammar for every modification and chromatin state; that remains a coverage gap.

BIF-07 covers computational reconstruction of large spatial maps, but not the full interactive-query objective. Highly accessible querying could be valuable; the supplied zero-latency formulation and the evidence reviewed do not establish a distinct unachieved revolutionary capability beyond scalable infrastructure and interface engineering.

original_dispositions.original_title: General predictive design of synthetic biological systems
original_dispositions.reason: Added as BIF-13, with whole-genome design separately retained as BIF-05. Performance is specified for named hosts rather than assumed to transfer to any chassis.

reconciliation_change_log.reason: Preserved their original concepts and IDs, their proposed completion criteria, and the distinction between molecular demonstrations and downstream clinical or engineering outcomes. Source-access failures in the follow-up are explicitly marked.

Added cell-fate forecasting, interaction and affinity prediction, autonomous discovery, accessible complex-genome assembly, strain-resolved metagenomics, and genetic circuit/pathway design. Each offers a distinct potentially transformative capability, even where it overlaps a retained entry.
Replaced “perfect,” “any,” “no information loss,” and similar guarantees with demonstrations tied to available information, specified conditions, uncertainty and independent validation.

The supplied PLOS DOI resolves to an article on spatially heterogeneous behavior and infectious-disease dynamics, not the claimed computational-biology editorial series. The ISMB URL returned 404; the supplied Nature URL failed to fetch, and the Genome Biology and ELIXIR URLs were inaccessible in this review. Those failures do not prove the pages never existed, but the supplied citations do not establish the historical answer’s claim that named sources endorsed all ten frontiers.
